Raphael, God heals, guided Tobias and cured his father’s blindness. In England the day has long been kept as Michaelmas, a quarter day and the start of the autumn term.
Saints Michael, Gabriel and Raphael · Life

The Church teaches that the angels are real, spiritual creatures who serve God and watch over us. Scripture names three. Michael appears in Daniel as the great prince who stands guard over God’s people, in the Letter of Jude disputing with the devil, and in the Apocalypse casting the dragon out of heaven. Gabriel is sent to Daniel to explain his visions, to Zechariah in the Temple to announce the birth of John the Baptist, and to Nazareth to greet Mary. Raphael, in the Book of Tobit, travels in disguise with the young Tobias, protects him and heals his father, then reveals himself as one of the seven who stand before the Lord. The date recalls the dedication of a basilica of Saint Michael on the Via Salaria near Rome in the early centuries. Since 1970 the three archangels have shared one feast.
Saints Michael, Gabriel and Raphael · Prayer to

Saint Michael, defend us in the battle against evil. Saint Gabriel, help us to hear the word of God and answer it as Mary did. Saint Raphael, guide us on our journeys and bring healing to the sick. Holy archangels, and my own guardian angel, keep me close to God this day and all the days of my life. Amen.
Saints Michael, Gabriel and Raphael · Prayer

Saint Michael the Archangel, defend us in battle. Be our protection against the wickedness and snares of the devil. May God rebuke him, we humbly pray; and do thou, O Prince of the heavenly host, by the power of God, thrust into hell Satan and all the evil spirits who wander through the world for the ruin of souls. Amen.
Saints Michael, Gabriel and Raphael · Meditation
Michael’s name is a question: who is like God? Is there anything in your life that you have set up as though it were God?

The greatest biblical scholar of the early Church. A brilliant, prickly priest from Dalmatia, he learned Hebrew in the Syrian desert, served Pope Damasus in Rome, and spent his last thirty-four years in Bethlehem translating the Scriptures into Latin. His Vulgate was the Bible of the Western Church for more than a thousand years.

Jerome was born at Stridon, on the borders of Dalmatia, and studied in Rome, where he was baptised. A great lover of the pagan classics, he later told of a dream in which he was judged a Ciceronian rather than a Christian. He tried the hermit’s life in the desert of Chalcis and there learned Hebrew from a Jewish convert. Ordained priest at Antioch, he came to Rome in 382 and became secretary to Pope Damasus, who asked him to revise the Latin Gospels. There he guided a circle of devout Roman women, among them Paula and her daughter Eustochium. After Damasus died he left for the Holy Land, and from 386 lived at Bethlehem, where Paula built monasteries for men and women. He translated most of the Old Testament from the Hebrew, wrote commentaries and letters, and quarrelled fiercely with his critics. He died at Bethlehem in 420.

Saint Jerome, you gave your life to the word of God and fought your own fierce temper all your days. Pray for translators, scholars and all who teach the Scriptures, and for me, that I may read the Bible daily, love it as you did, and bring my faults humbly to the Lord. Amen.

O God, Who graciously gave Your Church blessed Jerome, Your Confessor and peerless teacher, to explain the Holy Scriptures, grant, we beseech You, that, with the help of his merits and by Your assistance, we may be able to put into practice what he has taught us by his life and works. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Ignorance of the Scriptures is ignorance of Christ. How well do you know the Gospels, and how could you come to know them better?

A celebrated teacher at Reims who turned down a bishopric to seek God in silence. In 1084 he and six companions settled in the mountains of the Chartreuse, near Grenoble, and founded the Carthusians, monks who live as hermits in community. The order has never needed reform, it is said, because it was never deformed.

Born in Cologne around 1030, Bruno became master of the cathedral school at Reims, where one of his pupils later became Pope Urban II. He stood against a simoniac archbishop and lost his post for it. In 1084, with six companions, he went to Bishop Hugh of Grenoble, who had dreamed of seven stars guiding him to a wild valley in the Alps. There they built the Grande Chartreuse. Called to Rome by his old pupil, Bruno longed for solitude and was allowed to found a second hermitage at La Torre in Calabria, where he died in 1101. He was never formally canonised; his cult was approved in 1514.

Saint Bruno, you left honours and learning to seek God alone in the silence of the mountains. Teach me to love silence, to guard my heart from noise and distraction, and to find in stillness the God who speaks there. Pray for me, that I may seek Him first. Amen.

May we be aided by the intercession of St. Bruno, Your Confessor, we beseech You, O Lord; that we, who have grievously offended Your Majesty by sin, may, by his merits and prayers, obtain forgiveness for our offenses. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Stat crux dum volvitur orbis: the cross stands still while the world turns. Find ten minutes of silence today and let the world turn without you.
Our Lady of the Rosary · Life

On 7 October 1571 a Christian fleet defeated the Ottoman navy at Lepanto, while confraternities across Europe prayed the Rosary at Pope Pius V's request. He instituted a feast of Our Lady of Victory, later renamed Our Lady of the Rosary. October became the month of the Rosary.
Our Lady of the Rosary · Life

Tradition links the Rosary to Saint Dominic in the thirteenth century; it grew into its familiar form of fifteen decades by the sixteenth. Before the Battle of Lepanto in 1571, Pope Pius V asked all Christendom to pray it, and credited the victory to Our Lady's intercession. Gregory XIII gave the feast its present name in 1573. Popes since Leo XIII have written on the Rosary, and in 2002 John Paul II added the Luminous Mysteries.
Our Lady of the Rosary · Prayer to

Queen of the Most Holy Rosary, you walked with your Son from the crib to the cross to the glory of heaven. Take my hand as I pray, and let the mysteries of His life become the pattern of mine. Pray for us, that we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ. Amen.
Our Lady of the Rosary · Prayer

O God, Whose only-begotten Son, by His life, death and resurrection, has merited for us the grace of eternal salvation, grant, we beseech You, that, meditating on those mysteries in the most holy Rosary of the Blessed Virgin Mary, we may imitate what they contain and obtain what they promise. Through the same Christ our Lord…
Our Lady of the Rosary · Meditation
Pray one decade slowly today. Let each Hail Mary be one step beside Our Lady through the life of her Son.

A Swedish noblewoman, wife and mother of eight, who after her husband's death founded the Order of the Most Holy Saviour and spent her last twenty-four years in Rome, praying and pleading for the reform of the Church.

Bridget Birgersdotter was married at thirteen to Ulf Gudmarsson and bore eight children, among them Saint Catherine of Sweden. She served at the royal court and, after Ulf died in 1344, gave herself wholly to prayer. Her visions, recorded as the Revelations, called kings and popes to repentance and urged the papacy to return from Avignon to Rome. She founded a double monastery at Vadstena, went to Rome for the Jubilee of 1350 and never went home, dying there in 1373 after a pilgrimage to the Holy Land. John Paul II named her a patron saint of Europe in 1999.
Saint Bridget of Sweden · Prayer to

Saint Bridget, wife, mother and widow, you loved Christ crucified and were not afraid to speak the truth to the powerful. Help me to meditate on His Passion, to serve my family faithfully, and to pray for the renewal of the Church. Amen.

O Lord, our God, Who through your only-begotten Son revealed secrets to blessed Bridget, grant that through her kind intercession, we, Your servants, may rejoice and be glad in the revelation of Your eternal glory. Through the same Christ our Lord…
Bridget asked Christ how many blows He had suffered, and spent her life in gratitude for each one. Look at a crucifix today and thank Him for one wound in particular.

The leading Anglican thinker of his age, Newman followed his study of the early Church into the Catholic Church in 1845, at great personal cost. He founded the Birmingham Oratory, wrote The Idea of a University and The Dream of Gerontius, and was made a cardinal in 1879. He was canonised in 2019.

Newman was the leading light of the Oxford Movement, which sought to recover the Catholic heritage of the Church of England. His study of the Fathers led him, slowly and painfully, to conclude that the Catholic Church was the Church they knew. On 9 October 1845, the date of his feast, he was received by Blessed Dominic Barberi at Littlemore. He lost friends, position and income. As an Oratorian in Birmingham he preached, taught, founded a school and wrote the Apologia pro Vita Sua in reply to a public attack on his honesty. Leo XIII made him a cardinal in 1879; his motto was Cor ad cor loquitur, heart speaks to heart. Benedict XVI beatified him in Birmingham in 2010.
Saint John Henry Newman · Prayer to

Saint John Henry, you followed the kindly Light through doubt and loss to the fullness of the faith. Pray for all who search for truth, for those who have drifted from the Church, and for me, that I may take the next step God shows me, and trust Him with the rest. Amen.

Lead, kindly Light, amid the encircling gloom, lead Thou me on! The night is dark, and I am far from home; lead Thou me on! Keep Thou my feet; I do not ask to see the distant scene; one step enough for me.
One step enough for me. What is the one step God is asking of you today?

A Carmelite nun who, after years of lukewarm prayer, was converted before an image of the wounded Christ. She reformed her order, founding seventeen convents of the Discalced Carmelites, and wrote The Way of Perfection and The Interior Castle. In 1970 she became the first woman named a Doctor of the Church.

Teresa de Ahumada entered the Carmelite convent of the Incarnation at Ávila in 1535. For nearly twenty years her prayer was half-hearted, until in 1554 she was overcome before an image of the wounded Christ. From then on she lived a life of deep prayer and mystical graces. In 1562 she founded the small convent of Saint Joseph, returning to the strict original rule, and with Saint John of the Cross she carried the reform to the friars. She travelled Spain in a covered cart, founding convents in spite of illness and opposition, and wrote with humour and honesty about the soul's journey to God. She died at Alba de Tormes in 1582 and was canonised in 1622.
Saint Teresa of Ávila · Prayer to

Saint Teresa, you learned that God alone suffices. Teach me to pray as a friend speaks with a friend, to persevere when prayer is dry, and to keep a good humour on the way. Pray for me, that nothing may disturb me and nothing frighten me. Amen.
Let nothing disturb you, let nothing frighten you. All things are passing; God never changes. Patience obtains all things. Whoever has God lacks nothing. God alone suffices.
Prayer, Teresa said, is nothing else than an intimate sharing between friends. Speak to Christ today as a friend.

A Visitation nun at Paray-le-Monial to whom Christ revealed His Sacred Heart in a series of visions between 1673 and 1675. Doubted by her community, she persevered, and the devotion to the Sacred Heart spread through the whole Church, with its First Fridays and the feast of the Sacred Heart.

Margaret Mary entered the Visitation monastery at Paray-le-Monial in 1671. In a series of revelations Christ showed her His Heart, burning with love and wounded by ingratitude, and asked for a feast in its honour, for Communion on the first Friday of each month, and for an hour of prayer on Thursday nights in memory of His agony in Gethsemane. Her community thought her deluded until the Jesuit Saint Claude de la Colombière recognised the visions as genuine. The devotion she spread became one of the most widely loved in the Church. She was canonised in 1920.
Saint Margaret Mary Alacoque · Prayer to

Saint Margaret Mary, you saw the Heart that has so loved the world. Pray that my cold heart may be warmed by it, that I may make reparation for my sins and the sins of the world, and that I may rest in that Heart at the hour of my death. Amen.
Behold this Heart which has so loved men. Make an act of reparation today for indifference to that love.

Bishop of Antioch, taken under guard to Rome to be thrown to the beasts. On the way he wrote seven letters to the churches, the earliest witness outside Scripture to bishops, the Eucharist and the name 'Catholic Church'.

Ignatius was the third bishop of Antioch, where the disciples were first called Christians. Arrested under Trajan around 107, he was taken in chains across Asia Minor to Rome. On the way he wrote seven letters, to the Ephesians, Magnesians, Trallians, Romans, Philadelphians and Smyrnaeans, and to Bishop Polycarp. They are the earliest writings we have that speak of bishops, priests and deacons, of the Eucharist as the flesh of Christ, and of 'the Catholic Church'. He begged the Christians of Rome not to try to save him. He died in the arena.
Saint Ignatius of Antioch · Prayer to

Saint Ignatius, you went to your death longing to be wheat ground into the bread of Christ. Pray that I may love the Eucharist as you did, stay close to the Church, and not shrink from what following Christ will cost. Amen.
I am the wheat of God, and I am ground by the teeth of wild beasts, that I may be found the pure bread of Christ. What in you does God wish to grind into bread?

A Greek physician and companion of Saint Paul who wrote the third Gospel and the Acts of the Apostles. Only Luke gives us the Annunciation, the Visitation, the Magnificat, the Benedictus, the shepherds, the Prodigal Son and the Good Samaritan. Tradition says he painted the first icon of the Virgin.

Saint Paul calls him 'Luke, the most dear physician'. A Gentile, probably from Antioch, Luke travelled with Paul, and the 'we' passages of Acts are his eyewitness account. He wrote his Gospel 'in order', having carefully traced everything from the beginning, and his pages carry the infancy of Christ, the parables of mercy and the canticles the Church still prays every day. He is the patron of physicians, surgeons and artists.
Saint Luke the Evangelist · Prayer to

Saint Luke, physician and evangelist, you wrote of the mercy of God for the poor and the lost. Pray for all who care for the sick, for doctors and nurses, and for me, that I may know myself found by the Shepherd who came to seek the lost. Amen.

O Lord, we beseech You, that Luke, Your holy Evangelist, who for the honor of Your name bore continually in his body the suffering of the cross, may intercede in our behalf. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Read Luke 15 slowly today, the lost sheep, the lost coin and the lost son.

Karol Wojtyła, actor, philosopher and bishop of Kraków, was elected pope in 1978, the first non-Italian in 455 years. He helped bring down communism in Eastern Europe, travelled to 129 countries, gave the Church the Theology of the Body and the Catechism, and bore his long final illness in public.

Born in Wadowice in 1920, Karol Wojtyła lost his mother, brother and father by the age of twenty. Under Nazi occupation he worked in a quarry, acted in an underground theatre and studied secretly for the priesthood. As bishop and archbishop of Kraków he defended the Church against the communist regime. Elected pope in 1978, he travelled the world, began World Youth Day, survived an assassin's bullet in 1981 and visited the gunman in prison to forgive him. He established Divine Mercy Sunday, gave the Church the Catechism, and died on its vigil in 2005. He was canonised in 2014.
Saint John Paul II · Prayer to

Saint John Paul, you told the world not to be afraid. Pray for me in my fears, for families and young people, and for the Church you loved. Help me to open wide the doors of my life to Christ, and to trust in His mercy. Amen.
Do not be afraid. Open wide the doors for Christ. Which door have you kept shut?

Two of the Twelve, kept together because tradition holds that they preached in Persia and were martyred there together. Simon is called the Zealot; Jude, also named Thaddeus, wrote the short letter that bears his name and is the patron of hopeless causes.

Simon is called the Zealot, perhaps because he had belonged to the party that resisted Rome, perhaps for his zeal. Jude, also called Thaddeus, is the apostle who asked Christ at the Last Supper why He would show Himself to them and not to the world. He wrote the short Letter of Jude, urging the faithful to 'contend for the faith once delivered to the saints'. Western tradition holds that the two preached together in Persia and were martyred there.
Saints Simon and Jude · Prayer to

Saint Jude, faithful apostle and patron of things despaired of, I bring you what I cannot fix. Pray for me in this need, and teach me to trust in the God for whom nothing is impossible. Saint Simon, pray that my zeal may be for Christ alone. Amen.

O God, Who have given us a way of coming to know Your name through Your blessed Apostles Simon and Jude, grant us to honor their everlasting glory by becoming more holy and to become more holy by honoring it. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Bring to Saint Jude the situation you have given up on.

The Church honours in one feast all who have reached heaven, the great multitude which no man could number, most of them known only to God. The feast was fixed on 1 November in the eighth century and is a holy day of obligation.

The early Church kept the feasts of the martyrs on the anniversaries of their deaths. As their number grew beyond counting, a common feast emerged. In 609 Pope Boniface IV dedicated the Pantheon in Rome to Our Lady and all the martyrs, and in the eighth century Gregory III dedicated a chapel in Saint Peter's to all the saints on 1 November. Gregory IV extended the feast to the whole Church. It honours the saints we know and the vast company we do not, many of them ordinary men and women.

All you holy men and women, saints of God, pray for us. You have finished the race; help us to run it. Win for us the grace to become what God made us to be, and to join you in the vision of His face. Amen.

Almighty, eternal God, Who granted us to honor the merits of all Your Saints in a single solemn festival, bestow on us, we beseech You, through their manifold intercession, that abundance of Your mercy for which we yearn. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Holiness is not for a few. Ask one saint to be your companion this month.

The day after All Saints the Church prays for all who have died in God's friendship but still await purification. Priests may offer three Masses today. Through November Catholics visit graves and pray for their dead.

The custom of praying for the dead is older than Christianity; Judas Maccabeus 'made atonement for the dead, that they might be delivered from their sin'. Saint Odilo, abbot of Cluny, ordered a day of prayer for all the faithful departed around 998, and it spread through the whole Church. In 1915 Benedict XV allowed every priest to offer three Masses today, because of the dead of the First World War.

O Lord, by whose mercy the souls of the faithful find rest, grant to all my family, friends and benefactors who have died the forgiveness of their sins and the light of your face. Holy souls in purgatory, pray for us, and remember us when you come into your kingdom. Amen.
Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon them. May they rest in peace. Amen.
Name your dead before God today, one by one.

Son of a Spanish nobleman and a freed slave, Martin was a Dominican lay brother who served as barber, infirmarian and almoner. He cared for the sick, the poor, slaves and even animals, and was known for his humility and his gift of healing.

Martin was born in Lima in 1579 to Juan de Porres, a Spanish nobleman, and Ana Velázquez, a freed black woman from Panama. His father was slow to acknowledge him, and the boy grew up poor. He was apprenticed to a barber-surgeon and learned to dress wounds and prepare remedies. At about fifteen he went to the Dominican priory of the Holy Rosary, where the law of the time allowed a man of his birth only to serve as a lay helper; in 1603 he was professed as a lay brother. He swept, shaved, nursed and begged alms, setting up care for orphans and the sick poor of the city. He was a friend of Saint Rose of Lima, and many stories tell of his healings and his gentleness with animals. He died in 1639 and was canonised by John XXIII in 1962.
Saint Martin de Porres · Prayer to

Saint Martin de Porres, you were looked down on and answered with humble love, serving the sick, the poor and the forgotten of Lima. Pray for all who suffer because of their race or birth, and for me, that I may see Christ in each person I meet and serve Him gladly in the lowliest tasks. Amen.
He called himself 'the mulatto dog'. Do one hidden act of service today that no one will thank you for.

Nephew of Pope Pius IV and cardinal archbishop of Milan, he led the reform of the Church after the Council of Trent, founding seminaries and visiting every parish of his huge diocese. In the plague of 1576 he stayed in the city to nurse the sick when the governor fled.

Charles was born in 1538 at the castle of Arona on Lake Maggiore. When his uncle became Pope Pius IV in 1559, he made Charles a cardinal at twenty-one, administrator of the archdiocese of Milan and his chief assistant in Rome. Charles helped bring the Council of Trent to its close in 1563 and oversaw the Roman Catechism that followed it. The sudden death of his elder brother turned him to a more serious life; he was ordained priest and bishop and in 1566 went to live in Milan, which had not had a resident archbishop for decades. He held synods, founded seminaries, taught the catechism to children and visited remote Alpine parishes on foot. In 1569 a member of a religious order he was reforming shot at him while he prayed; he was unhurt. Worn out by work and penance, he died in 1584, aged forty-six.

Saint Charles, shepherd of Milan, you spent yourself for the reform of the Church and did not abandon your people in the plague. Pray for bishops and priests, that they may be faithful and fearless, and for me, that I may begin the renewal of the Church with the conversion of my own heart. Amen.

Safeguard Your Church, O Lord, under the continual protection of St. Charles, Your Confessor and Bishop, so that just as his concern for his flock made him glorious, so his intercession may make us ever fervent in loving You. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Reform begins at home. Choose one habit to amend this week.
Dedication of the Lateran Basilica · Life

Saint John Lateran, not Saint Peter's, is the cathedral of the Pope as Bishop of Rome, 'mother and head of all the churches of the city and the world'. It was dedicated by Pope Sylvester in 324, soon after the Church was freed from persecution.
Dedication of the Lateran Basilica · Life

The Lateran takes its name from the Laterani, a Roman family whose palace passed to the emperor Constantine. After he ended the persecution, Constantine gave the property to the Bishop of Rome, and a great basilica was built beside it and dedicated to Christ the Saviour; later the two Saints John, the Baptist and the Evangelist, were added to its title. For about a thousand years the popes lived at the Lateran, and five general councils of the Church met there, including the Fourth Lateran Council of 1215. The basilica has been ruined by earthquake and fire and rebuilt more than once; its present façade dates from the eighteenth century. The feast was extended to the whole Church as a sign of love and unity with the See of Peter.
Dedication of the Lateran Basilica · Prayer to

Lord God, you build your Church from living stones, chosen and precious. As we honour the cathedral of the Bishop of Rome, unite us more closely with the Holy Father and with one another. Make my own heart a fit dwelling for your Spirit, and keep every parish church a house of prayer for all peoples. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
Dedication of the Lateran Basilica · Meditation
You are God's temple. Pray for your own parish church and its priest today.

Pope at a time of collapse, Leo defined the Church's faith that Christ is one Person in two natures, a teaching the Council of Chalcedon received with the cry 'Peter has spoken through Leo'. He met Attila the Hun outside Rome and persuaded him to turn back.

Leo was a deacon of the Roman Church, trusted with delicate missions, and was away in Gaul when he was elected pope in 440. In 449 he sent his Tome to Bishop Flavian of Constantinople, setting out the faith that the one Christ is truly God and truly man, without confusion and without division. When a council at Ephesus that year rejected it by violence, Leo called it a robbery; two years later the Council of Chalcedon received his teaching. In 452 he went out to meet Attila near Mantua and the Huns withdrew from Italy. In 455 he could not prevent the Vandals from sacking Rome, but he persuaded their king to spare the city from burning and slaughter. Nearly a hundred of his sermons survive, clear and dignified. He died in 461 and was named a Doctor of the Church in 1754.
Saint Leo the Great · Prayer to

Saint Leo, faithful successor of Peter, you taught the Church to confess Christ as true God and true man, and you stood before invaders for your people. Pray that I may hold the faith clearly and humbly, remember the dignity God has given me, and not lose courage when the world around me is shaken. Amen.
Christian, remember your dignity. What would change if you believed it today?

A Roman soldier who, at the gates of Amiens, cut his cloak in half for a freezing beggar and that night saw Christ wearing it. He became a monk and bishop of Tours, one of the first saints venerated who was not a martyr. His feast fell on the day the 1918 Armistice was signed.

Martin was born around 316 at Sabaria in Pannonia, in present-day Hungary, the son of an army officer, and grew up at Pavia. Drawn to Christ as a boy, he was enrolled in the cavalry at fifteen. After he shared his cloak with the beggar at Amiens he was baptised, and some time later he left the army, telling the emperor that he was now a soldier of Christ. He became a disciple of Saint Hilary of Poitiers and founded at Ligugé the first monastery known in Gaul. In 371 the people of Tours chose him as their bishop against his will. He lived as a monk at Marmoutier outside the city, travelled the countryside preaching, and was known for his care of prisoners and the poor. He died at Candes in 397. His life was written by his friend Sulpicius Severus.
Saint Martin of Tours · Prayer to

Saint Martin, soldier of Christ, you saw the Lord in a freezing beggar and gave him half of what you had. Pray for soldiers and for all who suffer the cost of war, and for me, that I may not pass by the poor but share with them freely, as Christ has shared Himself with me. Amen.

O God, Who see that we cannot survive by any power of our own, mercifully grant that, by the intercession of blessed Martin, Your Confessor and Bishop, we may be made safe from all harm. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Whom will you give half your cloak to this week?
A Dominican friar and bishop who mastered every science of his day, from theology to botany and astronomy, and taught Thomas Aquinas. He is the patron saint of scientists.

Albert was born around 1200 at Lauingen in Swabia and studied at Padua, where he joined the young Order of Preachers. He taught in Dominican houses across Germany and then at Paris and Cologne. Among his students was a large, silent Italian whom the others called the dumb ox; Albert is said to have replied that the ox's bellowing would one day be heard throughout the world. The student was Thomas Aquinas. Albert wrote on almost every subject: Scripture and theology, the works of Aristotle, plants, animals, minerals and the stars, and he valued careful observation. In 1260 he was made bishop of Regensburg and resigned after two years to return to teaching. In old age he defended the teaching of Thomas, who had died before him. He died at Cologne in 1280 and was canonised and named a Doctor of the Church in 1931.
Saint Albert the Great · Prayer to

Saint Albert, you studied the works of God with patience and wonder and saw no quarrel between faith and reason. Pray for scientists, teachers and students, that they may seek the truth honestly and humbly. Help me to use my mind in God's service and to give Him thanks for all that I learn. Amen.

O God, Who made blessed Albert, Your Bishop and Doctor, eminent in the submission of human wisdom to divine faith, grant us, we beseech You, so to follow the path of his teaching that we may enjoy perfect light in heaven. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Faith and reason are two wings. Learn one new thing today and thank God for it.

An English princess who married King Malcolm III of Scotland. She reformed the Church in Scotland, founded the abbey at Dunfermline and the Queen's Ferry for pilgrims to Saint Andrews, and fed the poor at her own table before she ate.

Margaret was born around 1045 in Hungary, where her father, an English prince, lived in exile; she was a granddaughter of King Edmund Ironside. The family came to England in 1057, and after the Norman Conquest they fled north. About 1070 she married Malcolm III of Scotland. Of their eight children, three sons became kings of Scots and a daughter became queen of England. Her confessor Turgot, who wrote her life, tells that she rose at night to pray, read the Scriptures, and washed the feet of the poor and fed orphans before taking her own meal. She brought Benedictine monks from Canterbury to Dunfermline and encouraged councils that brought Scottish customs for Lent and Easter into line with the wider Church. Her small Gospel book, once dropped in a river and found undamaged, survives in Oxford. She died in 1093, days after her husband and eldest son were killed in battle.
Saint Margaret of Scotland · Prayer to

Saint Margaret, wife, mother and queen, you made your household a place of prayer and your table a place of welcome for the poor. Pray for husbands and wives, for parents and children, and for the peoples of Scotland and England. Help me to serve those I live with, patiently and gladly. Amen.
Holiness in marriage and family life: do one thing today for those you live with.

A king's daughter and a landgravine who, widowed at twenty, gave her wealth to build a hospital at Marburg and served the sick there herself. She died at twenty-four. Legend says bread she carried to the poor turned to roses when her husband asked to see it.

Elizabeth was born in 1207, a daughter of King Andrew II of Hungary, and at four was sent to the Wartburg castle to be raised with Louis of Thuringia, her future husband. They married when she was fourteen and loved each other deeply; they had three children. Influenced by the Franciscan friars newly come to Germany, she gave generously to the poor, and in a famine she opened the granaries while Louis was away. In 1227 Louis died of fever on his way to the Crusade. Elizabeth left the court, made provision for her children and took the habit of the Franciscan Third Order. With her dowry she built a hospital at Marburg in honour of Saint Francis and nursed the sick there with her own hands, under the strict direction of Conrad of Marburg. She died in 1231 and was canonised four years later.
Saint Elizabeth of Hungary · Prayer to

Saint Elizabeth, you were a princess who chose to be a servant, and you found Christ in the sick and the hungry. Pray for all who care for the suffering, for widows and the bereaved, and for me, that I may hold loosely to what I own and give freely to those in need. Amen.
Give something today that costs you.
The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary · Life

An ancient tradition tells that Joachim and Anne brought Mary as a small child to the Temple in Jerusalem to be offered to God. The feast honours her total dedication to God from the beginning of her life.
The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary · Life

The story of Mary's presentation comes from the Protoevangelium of James, a second-century writing not part of Scripture. It tells that Joachim and Anne, who had long been childless, brought their daughter at the age of three to the Temple, where she was received by the priest and lived in prayer until her betrothal to Joseph. The Church does not vouch for these details, but honours the truth they point to: that Mary belonged wholly to God from the beginning. The feast began in Jerusalem with the dedication of the New Church of Saint Mary in 543. It is one of the great feasts of the Eastern Churches, and spread in the West from the fourteenth century. Since 1953 the day has also been kept as a day of prayer for enclosed contemplative nuns.
The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary · Prayer to

Holy Mary, from your earliest years you were given wholly to God and kept nothing back. Pray for me, that I may offer myself to Him without reserve, as I am today. Pray for all who live hidden lives of prayer in the cloister, and keep us faithful to the Lord who has called us. Amen.
The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary · Prayer

O God, by Whose will the blessed Mary, ever Virgin, the dwelling place of the Holy Spirit, was on this day presented in the temple, grant, we beseech You, that by her intercession we may be found worthy to be brought into the temple of Your glory. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen. eiusdem
The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary · Meditation
Offer yourself again to God today, as you are.

A Roman virgin and martyr whose name is said in the Roman Canon. The story of her martyrdom says she sang to God in her heart, and so she became the patron of music and musicians. Her body was found incorrupt in 1599.

Cecilia was venerated in Rome from early times, and her name stands in the Roman Canon of the Mass. The story of her life comes from her Acts, written long after her death and largely legendary. They tell that she was a Christian of noble family who had vowed her virginity to God and was married against her will to Valerian, a pagan. On their wedding night she told him of her vow and of the angel who guarded her; Valerian was baptised, and with his brother Tiburtius was martyred. Cecilia was then condemned, survived an attempt to suffocate her in the bath of her house, and died of wounds from the sword. The church of Santa Cecilia in Trastevere is said to stand on the site of her home. She became the patron of musicians because an antiphon speaks of music played at her wedding.

Saint Cecilia, virgin and martyr, you sang to the Lord in your heart while the music of the world played around you. Pray for musicians and all who lead the Church's song, and for me, that my whole life may become a hymn of praise, faithful to Christ in every trial. Amen.

O God, Who gladden us by the annual feast of blessed Cecilia, Your Virgin and Martyr, grant, we beseech You, that we may by virtuous conduct follow her whom we venerate in this sacred rite. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Sing, or listen to, one piece of sacred music today with full attention.

A learned young woman of Alexandria who, tradition says, out-argued fifty pagan philosophers sent by the emperor and converted them. Sentenced to be broken on a spiked wheel, which shattered at her touch, she was beheaded. She was one of the voices heard by Saint Joan of Arc.

Catherine has been loved since at least the eighth century, but almost nothing about her can be shown from history, and her story belongs to tradition. It tells that she was a young woman of noble birth and great learning in Alexandria who was converted to Christ. When the emperor persecuted the Christians she confronted him, and he summoned fifty philosophers to refute her; she won them to the faith, and they were put to death. Refusing his offer of marriage, she was condemned to a wheel set with spikes, which broke apart, and was beheaded. Her body, it is said, was carried by angels to Mount Sinai, where the ancient monastery bears her name. She was counted among the Fourteen Holy Helpers. Removed from the general calendar in 1969 for lack of historical evidence, her memorial was restored in 2002.
Saint Catherine of Alexandria · Prayer to

Saint Catherine, tradition remembers you as wise and fearless, a young woman who defended the faith before the powerful. Pray for students, teachers and philosophers, that they may seek and love the truth. Help me to understand my faith well and to speak of it with gentleness and courage when I am questioned. Amen.

O God, Who gave the law to Moses on Sinai's height and through your holy angels miraculously placed there the body of blessed Catherine, Your Virgin and Martyr; grant, we beseech You, that by her merits and intercession we may reach that towering eminence which is Christ. Who livest and reignest with God the Father…
Love the truth enough to learn it well.

A fisherman of Bethsaida, disciple of John the Baptist, and the first apostle called by Christ. He brought his brother Simon Peter to Jesus. Tradition says he was crucified on an X-shaped cross at Patras in Greece, the saltire of Scotland's flag.

Andrew was a fisherman from Bethsaida who worked with his brother Simon on the Sea of Galilee. Saint John's Gospel tells that he was a disciple of John the Baptist, and that when the Baptist pointed to Jesus as the Lamb of God, Andrew followed Him and asked where He was staying. 'Come and see,' Jesus answered, and Andrew spent the day with Him. He went at once to tell Simon, 'We have found the Messiah.' Later it was Andrew who found the boy with five barley loaves and two fish, and who, with Philip, brought some Greeks to Jesus. Tradition holds that he preached around the Black Sea and in Greece and was crucified at Patras. He is the patron of Scotland, of Greece and of the Church of Constantinople, and his feast is a day of friendship between Rome and the Orthodox.
Saint Andrew the Apostle · Prayer to

Saint Andrew, you left your nets when Christ called and went at once to bring your brother to Him. Pray for me, that I may follow the Lord without delay and share Him with those I love. Pray for the unity of Christians of East and West, and for the people of Scotland. Amen.
We humbly pray Your majesty, O Lord, that, as blessed Andrew was a preacher and ruler in Your Church, so he may always intercede for us with You. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Andrew's first act as a disciple was to bring someone else to Jesus. Whom will you bring?

One of the first companions of Saint Ignatius of Loyola, he became the greatest missionary since Saint Paul, preaching in India, the Malay archipelago and Japan, and baptising tens of thousands. He died on an island off the coast of China, waiting to enter it.

Francis was born in 1506 at the castle of Xavier in Navarre. At the University of Paris he shared rooms with Peter Faber and then with Ignatius of Loyola, who slowly won the ambitious young teacher for Christ. In 1534 the friends made their vows at Montmartre, the beginning of the Society of Jesus. In 1541, at the request of the King of Portugal, Francis sailed for the Indies and reached Goa the next year. He taught the faith to the fishing people of southern India, then worked in Malacca and the Moluccas, ringing a bell in the streets to call children to the catechism. In 1549 he reached Japan and spent two years there, adapting his ways to its culture. Hoping to enter China, he fell ill on the island of Shangchuan and died there in 1552. His body lies at Goa.

Saint Francis Xavier, you gave up your ambitions to carry the Gospel to the ends of the earth. Pray for missionaries, and for all who have not yet heard of Christ. Stir up in me a zeal for souls, and help me to bring the love of God to the people around me, wherever He sends me. Amen.

O God, You Who were pleased to gather into Your Church the peoples of the Indies by the preaching and miracles of blessed Francis, mercifully grant that we, who honor his glorious merits, may also imitate the example of his virtues. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
What does it profit a man to gain the whole world and lose his soul? Ignatius asked him this until he gave his life away.

Bishop of Myra in Asia Minor, remembered for secretly giving three bags of gold to save three poor girls from ruin by throwing them through a window at night. From that hidden charity came Santa Claus.

Nicholas was bishop of Myra in Lycia, on the south coast of present-day Turkey, in the fourth century. Few facts about him are certain, but his cult was strong in East and West from early times. Tradition says he was born at Patara to wealthy Christian parents, gave away his inheritance, suffered imprisonment in the persecution under Diocletian and attended the Council of Nicaea. Other stories tell how he saved three innocent men from execution and calmed a storm for sailors. In 1087 sailors from Bari carried his relics from Myra to their own city, where they rest in the Basilica of San Nicola. He is the patron of children, sailors and Russia. The Dutch kept his feast with gifts for children as Sinterklaas, and from that custom came Santa Claus.

Saint Nicholas, generous shepherd, you gave in secret to save the poor from shame and despair. Pray for children, for families in need, and for all who travel by sea. Teach me to give without being seen, and to prepare for Christmas with a heart turned towards others. Amen.

O God, You who made the holy Bishop Nicholas renowned for countless miracles, grant, we beseech You, that by his merits and prayers we may be saved from the fires of hell. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

A Roman governor acclaimed bishop of Milan by the people while still unbaptised. He wrote hymns still sung in the Divine Office, defended the Church against emperors, and his preaching helped bring Saint Augustine to faith.

Ambrose was born around 340 at Trier, the son of a high Roman official, and trained in law. As governor of the province around Milan he went to the cathedral in 374 to keep order at a bitter election for bishop. Tradition says a child's voice cried 'Ambrose for bishop', and the crowd took it up. He was still a catechumen; within a week he was baptised and ordained, and he was consecrated on 7 December. He gave his wealth to the poor and studied the Scriptures and the Greek Fathers. When the empress Justina demanded a church for the Arians, he occupied it with his people, teaching them hymns to sing through the night. He refused Communion to the emperor Theodosius until he did penance for a massacre at Thessalonica. At the Easter Vigil of 387 he baptised Augustine. He died on Holy Saturday, 397.

Saint Ambrose, faithful bishop, you preached the word with power, sang the praises of God and stood firm before emperors. Pray for bishops and for all who teach the faith, and for me, that I may love the Scriptures, speak the truth with courage, and help others find their way to Christ. Amen.

O God, who didst give blessed Ambrósii to be thy people’s minister in eternal salvation; grant, we pray, that we who have him for teacher of life here on earth, may also deserve now that he is in heaven, to have him for an advocate. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Ambrose made an emperor do public penance. Where do you need to repent publicly, even in a small way?

The Church teaches that Mary, by a singular grace of God and in view of the merits of Christ, was preserved free from all stain of original sin from the first moment of her conception. Pius IX defined the dogma in 1854; four years later Our Lady told Bernadette at Lourdes, 'I am the Immaculate Conception.'

The feast of Mary's conception was kept in the East from about the eighth century, and in England it was celebrated at Winchester and Canterbury before the Norman Conquest. Theologians long debated how Mary could be free of original sin when all are redeemed by Christ. The Franciscan John Duns Scotus answered that she was redeemed in a more perfect way, preserved from sin rather than freed from it, in view of her Son's merits. Pope Sixtus IV approved the feast in 1476, and Clement XI extended it to the whole Church in 1708. On 8 December 1854 Pius IX defined the doctrine as revealed by God, in the bull Ineffabilis Deus. At Lourdes in 1858 the Lady told Bernadette her name, words the Church has approved as private revelation. In many countries today is a holy day of obligation.

Immaculate Virgin Mary, all fair and full of grace, God preserved you from every stain of sin to be the worthy Mother of His Son. Look kindly on me, a sinner. Help me to hate sin and love purity of heart, and lead me by your prayers to the Saviour who redeemed you first and redeems us all. Amen.
O Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to thee.
Tota pulchra es, Maria. Ask her to help you hate one particular sin.

In December 1531 the Virgin appeared to Juan Diego, a poor Aztec convert, on the hill of Tepeyac. As a sign for the bishop she filled his cloak with Castilian roses, and when he opened it her image was found printed on it. Millions were baptised in the years that followed.

Juan Diego was a Nahua man, born around 1474, who had been baptised by Franciscan missionaries a few years after the Spanish conquest of Mexico. On 9 December 1531, walking to Mass, he heard music on the hill of Tepeyac and saw a young woman who spoke to him in his own language and asked for a church to be built there. Bishop Juan de Zumárraga asked for a sign. On 12 December, hurrying to find a priest for his dying uncle, Juan Diego tried to avoid the hill, but the Lady met him, promised his uncle's healing and sent him to gather roses on its frozen summit. When he opened his cloak before the bishop, the roses fell and the image was there. The account was written down in Nahuatl, and the Church has approved the apparitions as private revelation. Juan Diego was canonised in 2002.
Our Lady of Guadalupe · Prayer to

Our Lady of Guadalupe, you came to a poor man and spoke to him tenderly in his own tongue. You are here, our mother. Take under your mantle the peoples of the Americas, the poor and the forgotten, mothers and their unborn children, and me in my troubles. Bring us all to your Son. Amen.
Am I not here, I who am your mother? Bring her your greatest worry.

A young Christian of Syracuse in Sicily who gave her dowry to the poor and was martyred under Diocletian. Her name means light, and her feast, near the darkest days of the year, is kept with candles, especially in Scandinavia. She is named in the Roman Canon.

Lucy was martyred at Syracuse in Sicily in the persecution under Diocletian, around 304, and an inscription from about 400 shows that her feast was already kept there. The details of her story come from later Acts. They tell that she was a young Christian of wealthy family who had resolved to give her life to God. Her mother, Eutychia, was ill, and the two went on pilgrimage to the tomb of Saint Agatha at Catania, where her mother was healed. Lucy then persuaded her to give the dowry to the poor. The man she had been promised to denounced her as a Christian. The governor ordered her taken to a place of shame, but tradition says she could not be moved, and she was killed by the sword. Later tradition linked her with the eyes, and she is the patron of the blind.

Saint Lucy, your name means light, and you gave away all you had for Christ. Pray for the blind and for all who live in darkness of body or soul. Keep the eyes of my heart clear, that I may see what God asks of me, and help me to be a small light for others in these dark days. Amen.

Graciously hear us, O God of our salvation; that as we rejoice in the festivity of blessed Luciæ Vírginis tuæ, we may be instructed in the affections of a loving devotion. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Be a light in someone's darkness today.
Saint John of the Cross · Life

A Carmelite friar who worked with Saint Teresa of Ávila to reform his order and was imprisoned by his own brothers for it. In a tiny cell in Toledo he wrote his greatest poetry. The Dark Night and The Living Flame of Love map the way of the soul to union with God.
Saint John of the Cross · Life

Juan de Yepes was born in 1542 at Fontiveros near Ávila. His father died young, and his mother brought up her sons in hard poverty. At Medina del Campo he worked in a hospital while studying with the Jesuits, and in 1563 he joined the Carmelites. Ordained in 1567, he was thinking of becoming a Carthusian when he met Teresa of Ávila, who persuaded him to help her reform. The next year at Duruelo he began the first house of the Discalced friars and took the name John of the Cross. In December 1577 friars opposed to the reform seized him and held him in their priory at Toledo, beaten and in darkness. There he composed much of the Spiritual Canticle. After nine months he escaped by night. In his last illness he was treated harshly by his own superior. He died at Úbeda in 1591 and was named a Doctor of the Church in 1926.
Saint John of the Cross · Prayer to

Saint John of the Cross, in a dark cell you found the living flame of God's love. Pray for all who walk through dryness, doubt or suffering, that they may trust that God is near. Teach me to let go of what holds me back from Him, and to seek Him above everything He gives. Amen.
Saint John of the Cross · Meditation
In the evening of life we shall be judged on love.

One of the seven deacons chosen by the apostles to serve the poor, Stephen was stoned to death in Jerusalem for his preaching, praying for his killers as he died. A young man named Saul held the cloaks of those who stoned him.

The Acts of the Apostles tells that when the Greek-speaking widows of Jerusalem were neglected in the daily distribution, the apostles chose seven men full of faith and the Holy Spirit to serve them, and Stephen was named first. He also worked wonders and preached with a wisdom his opponents could not answer. Accused falsely of speaking against the Temple and the Law, he was brought before the council, and his face seemed like the face of an angel. He answered with a long account of God's dealings with Israel, then cried out that he saw the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God. He was dragged out and stoned. 'Lord Jesus, receive my spirit,' he prayed, and fell asleep. The persecution that followed scattered the Church and carried the Gospel beyond Jerusalem. His relics were found in 415.

Saint Stephen, first martyr, you served the poor and bore witness to Christ, and you died praying for those who stoned you. Pray for deacons and for all who suffer for the faith. Give me a share of your courage and your forgiving heart, that I may love even those who wrong me. Amen.

Grant us, we beseech You, O Lord, to imitate what we celebrate, so that we may learn to love even our enemies; because we keep the anniversary of the invention of Him Who knew how to plead even for His persecutors with our Lord, Jesus Christ, Your Son. Who livest and reignest with God the Father…
Lord, do not hold this sin against them. Forgive someone today.

The beloved disciple, who leaned on the Lord's breast at the Last Supper, stood at the foot of the cross and took Mary into his home. He wrote the fourth Gospel, three letters and the Apocalypse, and is the only apostle believed not to have died a martyr.

John was a son of Zebedee and, with his brother James, a fisherman on the Sea of Galilee. Jesus called the brothers the sons of thunder, and once they wanted to call down fire on a Samaritan village that would not receive Him. With Peter and James, John saw the raising of Jairus's daughter, the Transfiguration and the agony in Gethsemane. Tradition identifies him with the disciple whom Jesus loved, who ran with Peter to the empty tomb and recognised the risen Lord on the shore. After Pentecost he preached with Peter in Jerusalem, and Paul names him one of the pillars of the Church. Tradition holds that he was exiled to Patmos and lived to great age at Ephesus, where he cared for Mary. On his feast wine is blessed, recalling a legend that he drank a poisoned cup unharmed.
Saint John the Apostle · Prayer to

Saint John, beloved disciple, you rested on the heart of Christ and stood by His cross with His mother. Pray that I may know how much I am loved by God, and learn to love in return. Take me with you into the mystery of the Word made flesh, and teach me to love my neighbour. Amen.

O Lord, graciously shed light upon Your Church, so that, enlightened by the teachings of blessed John, Your Apostle and Evangelist, she may gain Your everlasting rewards. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Little children, love one another. In old age, they say, this was all he would preach.
The children of Bethlehem killed by King Herod in his attempt to destroy the newborn Christ. The Church honours them as martyrs, who confessed Christ not by speaking but by dying.

Saint Matthew's Gospel tells that when the Magi did not return, King Herod, furious, ordered the killing of all the boys in Bethlehem and its district who were two years old or under, and that Joseph had already taken the Child and His mother to Egypt. Matthew sees in this the fulfilment of Jeremiah's words about Rachel weeping for her children. The deed fits what is known of Herod, who killed a wife and several of his own sons. Bethlehem was a small town, and the number of children was probably small, but each was a child known and loved. The Church has kept their feast since the fifth century, and they are honoured as martyrs who died not only for Christ but in His place. In England the day was once called Childermas.

Holy Innocents, little ones of Bethlehem, you gave your lives before you could speak His name. Pray for children who suffer violence, neglect or hunger, for children who have died, and for their grieving parents. Pray for all who hold power over the weak, that they may protect the smallest and most defenceless. Amen.

O God, Whose praise the Innocents, Your martyrs, this day proclaimed, not by speaking, but by dying, put to death in us all the wickedness of sin, so that Your faith which our tongue professes may be proclaimed also by our life. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Pray today for children who suffer, born and unborn.

Chancellor and friend of King Henry II, Thomas became Archbishop of Canterbury and defended the freedom of the Church against the king. Four knights murdered him in his own cathedral. Canterbury became one of the great pilgrim shrines of Europe.

Thomas was born in Cheapside, London, around 1120, to Norman parents. He entered the household of Theobald, Archbishop of Canterbury, who saw his talent, and in 1155 Henry II made him chancellor. Thomas served the king brilliantly, lived lavishly and became his close friend. In 1162 Henry had him made archbishop, expecting an ally. Instead Thomas resigned the chancellorship, took up a life of prayer and penance, and resisted the king's claim to try clergy in royal courts and control the Church's dealings with Rome. In 1164 he fled to France and spent six years in exile, for a time at the Cistercian abbey of Pontigny. He returned in December 1170. On 29 December four knights, taking angry words of the king as a command, killed him in his cathedral. He was canonised in 1173, and Henry did public penance at his tomb.

Saint Thomas of Canterbury, you turned from the favour of a king to serve the King of kings, and you died for the freedom of the Church. Pray for England and for all who hold authority, that they may govern justly. Give me courage to put God first, even at the cost of friendship or comfort. Amen.
Willing to die for the Church: what would you be willing to give up for her?
